title: PLACEHOLDER: Statistical Inference, written exam
instructions:
**PLACEHOLDER EXAM.** This file only proves that the pipeline works; replace it with real questions.

Answer in LaTeX. Write $...$ for inline maths and `\begin{align} ... \end{align}` for displayed derivations. Show every step: marks are given for the working, not only for the final answer.

questions.title: Exponential model (placeholder)
questions.text: Let $X_1,\dots,X_n$ be i.i.d. exponential with mean $\mu>0$, with density $f(x\mid\mu)=\mu^{-1}e^{-x/\mu}$ for $x>0$. Write $\bar X=n^{-1}\sum_i X_i$. Recall that $\E[X_1]=\mu$ and $\Var(X_1)=\mu^2$.

parts.text: Derive the maximum likelihood estimator of $\mu$, and verify that it is a maximum.

markingScheme.step: Score equation $-n/\mu+\mu^{-2}\sum_i x_i=0$ and solution $\hat\mu=\bar x$
Second derivative at $\hat\mu$ is $-n/\bar x^2<0$, so it is a maximum

parts.modelAnswer:
The log-likelihood is
$$\ell(\mu)=\sum_{i=1}^n\log f(x_i\mid\mu)=-n\log\mu-\frac1\mu\sum_{i=1}^n x_i .$$
Setting the score to zero,
$$\ell'(\mu)=-\frac n\mu+\frac1{\mu^2}\sum_i x_i=0\iff \mu=\bar x .$$
The second derivative is $\ell''(\mu)=\dfrac n{\mu^2}-\dfrac{2\sum_i x_i}{\mu^3}$, and at $\mu=\bar x$ it equals $\dfrac n{\bar x^2}-\dfrac{2n}{\bar x^2}=-\dfrac n{\bar x^2}<0$. Hence $\hat\mu=\bar X$ is the MLE.

parts.text: Compute the Fisher information $I_n(\mu)$ of the sample.
parts.modelAnswer:
From part (a), $\ell''(\mu)=n/\mu^2-2\sum_i X_i/\mu^3$. Since $\E[\sum_i X_i]=n\mu$,
$$\E[\ell''(\mu)]=\frac n{\mu^2}-\frac{2n\mu}{\mu^3}=-\frac n{\mu^2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad I_n(\mu)=-\E[\ell''(\mu)]=\frac n{\mu^2}.$$

parts.text: Show that $\bar X$ is unbiased for $\mu$ and attains the Cramér-Rao lower bound. Conclude that it is the UMVUE of $\mu$.

markingScheme.step: Cramér-Rao bound for unbiased estimators is $1/I_n(\mu)=\mu^2/n$
Variance equals the bound, so no unbiased estimator has smaller variance, hence UMVUE

parts.modelAnswer:
By linearity $\E[\bar X]=n^{-1}\sum_i\E[X_i]=\mu$, so $\bar X$ is unbiased. By independence,
$$\Var(\bar X)=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\Var(X_i)=\frac{n\mu^2}{n^2}=\frac{\mu^2}n .$$
The Cramér-Rao lower bound for any unbiased estimator of $\mu$ is $1/I_n(\mu)=\mu^2/n$ by part (b). Since $\Var(\bar X)$ equals this bound, every unbiased estimator $T$ has $\Var(T)\ge\mu^2/n=\Var(\bar X)$. Hence $\bar X$ is the uniformly minimum variance unbiased estimator of $\mu$. $\blacksquare$

parts.text: With $n=50$ and $\bar x=2.4$, give an approximate 95% confidence interval for $\mu$ based on the asymptotic normality of the MLE, using the plug-in standard error and $z_{0.975}=1.96$.
parts.modelAnswer:
The MLE is asymptotically $N(\mu,\,I_n(\mu)^{-1})$, so the plug-in standard error is $\hat\mu/\sqrt n=2.4/\sqrt{50}\approx0.3394$. The interval is
$$2.4\pm1.96\times0.3394\approx 2.4\pm0.665=(1.735,\;3.065).$$
